Enquiry 1: Four River Cradles & The Gift of the Nile — Why Did Ancient Egypt Flourish? (c. 3500–2700 BC)

Big Question: Where did the earliest river civilisations grow, and why did Ancient Egypt flourish beside the River Nile?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Civilisation (Civ-i-li-sa-tion) Inundation (In-un-da-tion) Kemet (Kem-et) Shaduf (Sha-duf) Papyrus (Pa-py-rus)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Mesopotamian Clay Cuneiform Tablet from Ancient Sumer (c. 3000 BC)
River Cradle Clue: Just like the Nile in Egypt, giant rivers in Sumer, the Indus Valley, and Shang China supplied water, soft mud, and boat transport!

1a. Inspect Source A. How did great rivers help early cities in Sumer and Egypt grow?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, pressing wedge marks into soft river clay helped early cities in Sumer and Egypt..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
King Narmer unites Upper and Lower Egypt wearing the Double Crown (c. 3100 BC)
Early river farming villages grow beside the Nile, Tigris/Euphrates, Indus, and Yellow River (c. 3500 BC)
Old Kingdom scribes and farmers expand shaduf canals along the Nile valley (c. 2700 BC)
Villagers harvest wild grain and papyrus reeds along marshy Nile banks (c. 4500 BC)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 2: Pyramids of Giza & The Great Sphinx — How Were Giant Stone Tombs Built? (c. 2670–2500 BC)

Big Question: Why and how did Old Kingdom Egyptians build giant stone pyramids and the Great Sphinx at Giza?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Pharaoh (Pha-raoh) Pyramid (Pyr-a-mid) Quarry (Quar-ry) Limestone (Lime-stone) Sphinx (Sphinx)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Giant Stepped Core Limestone Blocks of Pharaoh Khufu’s Great Pyramid at Giza (c. 2560 BC)
Archaeology Clue: Excavated bakeries, fish bones, and neat workers’ graves prove paid Egyptian crews—NOT whipped slaves—built Giza!

1a. Compare the visitors and blocks in Source A. What makes building this pyramid astonishing?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, the giant stepped limestone blocks of Khufu’s Great Pyramid show Egyptian crews..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Artisans at Deir el-Medina stage history’s first recorded strike over late rations (c. 1152 BC)
Architect Imhotep builds the six-tiered stone Step Pyramid for Djoser at Saqqara (c. 2650 BC)
Pharaoh Khafre’s workers carve the 73-metre Great Sphinx from Giza bedrock (c. 2520 BC)
Paid Egyptian crews raise the Great Pyramid of Khufu using 2.3 million stone blocks (c. 2560 BC)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 3: Scribes, Hieroglyphs & Everyday Life — How Did Ordinary Egyptians Live? (c. 2500–1200 BC)

Big Question: How did everyday life differ across Egypt’s social pyramid, and how did historians finally crack hieroglyphs?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Vizier (Vi-zier) Scribe (Scribe) Hieroglyphs (Hi-er-o-glyphs) Senet (Sen-et) Cartouche (Car-touche)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: The Rosetta Stone Carved in Three Scripts (Carved 196 BC, Discovered AD 1799)
Decipherment Clue (1822): Matching Greek royal names to oval hieroglyphic cartouches let Champollion read Ancient Egyptian sounds again!

1a. Look at the three bands on Source A. How did Champollion crack hieroglyphs in 1822?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, the three different scripts carved onto the Rosetta Stone allowed Champollion to..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Jean-François Champollion deciphers Egyptian hieroglyphs in Paris (AD 1822)
Early Egyptian scribes paint sacred hieroglyphs on temple walls and papyrus (c. 3100 BC)
Soldiers near Rashid (Rosetta) uncover the carved black Rosetta Stone slab (AD 1799)
Priests in Memphis carve a royal decree in three scripts onto the Rosetta Stone (196 BC)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 4: Gods, Mummies & Weighing the Heart — What Did Egyptians Believe About Death? (c. 2000–1000 BC)

Big Question: What did Ancient Egyptians believe happened after death, and why did they make mummies?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Polytheistic (Pol-y-the-is-tic) Mummification (Mum-mi-fi-ca-tion) Natron (Na-tron) Canopic Jars (Ca-nop-ic Jars) Shabti (Shab-ti)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Black & Gold Jackal Shrine Statue of Anubis (New Kingdom)
Afterlife Clue: Jackal-headed Anubis watched over mummification (natron salt & four canopic jars) and weighed the heart against Ma’at’s Feather!

1a. Look closely at Source A. Why was jackal-shaped Anubis placed inside royal tombs?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, the black-and-gold jackal shrine of Anubis guarded royal tombs because..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Scribe Hunefer’s painted Book of the Dead papyrus shows the Weighing of the Heart (c. 1275 BC)
Desert sand burials naturally dry early Egyptian bodies before stone tombs (c. 3400 BC)
New Kingdom embalmers perfect 70-day natron mummification and four canopic jars (c. 1500 BC)
Old Kingdom pyramid texts carve protective afterlife spells inside royal chambers (c. 2350 BC)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 5: Hatshepsut, Nefertiti & Ramesses II — Who Were Egypt's Mightiest New Kingdom Rulers? (c. 1500–1213 BC)

Big Question: What made Hatshepsut, Nefertiti, and Ramesses II three of Ancient Egypt's most remarkable New Kingdom rulers?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: New Kingdom (New King-dom) Expedition (Ex-pe-di-tion) Frankincense (Frank-in-cense) Chariot (Char-i-ot) Peace Treaty (Peace Trea-ty)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: Red Granite Sphinx Statue of Female Pharaoh Hatshepsut (c. 1470 BC)
Royal Power Clue: Hatshepsut ruled for twenty peaceful years not merely as queen consort, but crowned as full Pharaoh of Upper and Lower Egypt.

1a. Look closely at Hatshepsut’s chin and body in Source A. Why was she carved like this?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, carving female Pharaoh Hatshepsut as a royal granite sphinx with a beard shows..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
UNESCO engineers lift Abu Simbel’s giant cliff statues above rising Lake Nasser (AD 1968)
Female Pharaoh Hatshepsut sends five Red Sea ships to the Land of Punt (c. 1470 BC)
Ramesses II and the Hittites sign the world’s oldest surviving peace treaty (1258 BC)
Ramesses II clashes with Hittite war chariots at the Battle of Kadesh (1274 BC)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?

Enquiry 6: Tutankhamun's Tomb & Cleopatra VII — How Did Ancient Egypt End & Live On? (1332–30 BC & AD 1922)

Big Question: Why did Tutankhamun's hidden tomb survive until 1922, and how did Cleopatra VII's reign end pharaonic Egypt?
Name: _______________________
Date: ________________________
KEY WORDS: Valley of the Kings (Val-ley of the Kings) Excavation (Ex-ca-va-tion) Sarcophagus (Sar-coph-a-gus) Ptolemaic (Ptol-e-ma-ic) Dynasty (Dy-nas-ty)
TASK 1 Historical Evidence Detective • Inspect the Clue
Source A: 1923 Photograph of Howard Carter Inspecting Tutankhamun’s Golden Shrine (KV62)
KV62 Clue (1922): Hidden beneath later workmen’s huts, Tutankhamun’s small tomb held 5,398 fragile treasures needing careful conservation!

1a. Look at Howard Carter working in Source A. Why did recording KV62 take ten patient years?

Starter: "Looking closely at Source A, Howard Carter and his team spent ten patient years cataloguing KV62 because..."
TASK 2 Chronology Challenge • Number These Events from 1 (Earliest) to 4 (Latest)
Howard Carter and Egyptian dig foremen uncover Tutankhamun’s intact tomb KV62 (AD 1922)
Nine-year-old Tutankhamun becomes pharaoh and restores worship of Amun (c. 1332 BC)
Roman general Octavian defeats Cleopatra VII and Egypt becomes a Roman province (30 BC)
Scholar-queen Cleopatra VII takes the throne of Ptolemaic Alexandria (51 BC)

2b. Quick Explain: Which of these four events mattered most, and why?
